name: 000_korber_env_gp160
notes: signature: compute_neural_covariance_kernel(cross_attn, taxa_repr=None, mds_coords=None) -> (n, n). Reference hyphaeon/dating.py:78-118, lifted by ast and executed without importing hyphaeon (torch is bound into the namespace for the one body that needs it at call time). THE REAL ONE, and the reason this table's class is 1e-5 and not 1e-9: numpy matmuls the FLOAT32 inputs with sgemm (dating.py:96, 107), whose accumulation order is the BLAS implementation's, so no float64 port can be bit-exact. MEASURED: recomputing this same kernel in float64 from the same inputs moves it by max |delta| 1.954e-06. CONDITIONING, because no reader will guess it: mean_cross_attn's entries run 0.00611367 to 0.01823005, but after column centring max |a_c| = 0.00467723 and rms = 1.719807e-04 -- the correlation divides by a quantity about forty times smaller than the raw entries, which is why a 1e-8 perturbation of the attention shows up as 8e-6 in K. INVARIANTS a port must hold: unit diagonal, symmetry, and PSD -- the eigenvalues here run 0.003130989057219204 to 82.19852224418779, strictly positive, so the np.maximum(w, 0) clamps downstream at dating.py:1347 and 1490 never bind on this example.

name: 001_attention_only
notes: signature: compute_neural_covariance_kernel(cross_attn, taxa_repr=None). Reference hyphaeon/dating.py:78-118, lifted by ast and executed without importing hyphaeon (torch is bound into the namespace for the one body that needs it at call time). taxa_repr=None takes the unfused arm at dating.py:115 and K_neural IS K_attn. The application always supplies the embeddings, so this arm is dead on the product's path; it is three lines and it is pinned anyway.

name: 002_length_mismatch_ignores_repr
notes: signature: compute_neural_covariance_kernel(cross_attn, taxa_repr). Reference hyphaeon/dating.py:78-118, lifted by ast and executed without importing hyphaeon (torch is bound into the namespace for the one body that needs it at call time). `len(taxa_repr) == n` at dating.py:104 is a ROW count, and a mismatch SILENTLY drops the embedding half with no error and no flag -- the returned matrix is K_attn alone and looks exactly like a fused one. Pinned because a port that raised here, or that fused anyway, would both be defensible and both be wrong.

name: 003_constant_rows_zero_variance
notes: signature: compute_neural_covariance_kernel(cross_attn). Reference hyphaeon/dating.py:78-118, lifted by ast and executed without importing hyphaeon (torch is bound into the namespace for the one body that needs it at call time). every column is constant, so a_cov is identically zero, a_std is floored at sqrt(1e-12) = 1e-6 and a_denom = 1e-12 is NOT > 1e-12: the `where=` guard fails for every entry and np.divide leaves its `out` untouched. `out` is np.eye(n) (dating.py:99), so the answer is the IDENTITY -- ones on the diagonal, zeros off it -- and not a zero matrix. A port that wrote zeros, or that let 0/1e-12 through as 0.0, gets the off-diagonal right by accident and the diagonal right only because of the fill_diagonal on the next line.

name: 004_synthetic_n5_fused
notes: signature: compute_neural_covariance_kernel(cross_attn, taxa_repr). Reference hyphaeon/dating.py:78-118, lifted by ast and executed without importing hyphaeon (torch is bound into the namespace for the one body that needs it at call time). five taxa and three embedding dimensions, small enough to check by hand, with BOTH halves recorded so the 50/50 fusion at dating.py:113 can be verified as an average rather than inferred from the total. Row 4 of the embeddings is all zeros, so its centred row is the negated column mean and its correlations are still defined.
